trust_decision.summary: Decided nowhere at the pinned commit: verify_math_expression hands the caller's math strings straight to SymPy's eval-based parse_expr, with SymPy's default global namespace (full builtins) and only a five-name local_dict, so any expression text a caller supplies is executed as Python.

landing_point.why: The first parse_expr() call on the caller's 'expression' string is the single line where the advisory's remote-code-execution path lands; the second call eight lines later has the same shape.

fix_sites.module_kind: engine module / public library API (not wired to any registered MCP tool at the pinned commit)

fix_sites.entry_point: qwed_mcp.engines.safe_parser.safe_parse_expr (new module added by the fix; does not exist at the pinned commit)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only arguable dismissal is reachability: no registered MCP tool calls the math engine at the pinned commit (tools.py:348-384 lists only execute_python_code and verification_status; README.md:82 says verify_math was removed in v0.2.0), so a solver could call verify_math_expression dead library code and harden nothing.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The documented public input format is loose math notation: 'x^2' (caret power, rewritten to '**' before parsing) and '2x' (implicit multiplication, supplied by implicit_multiplication_application in the transformation tuple). An over-broad fix that drops or narrows the transformation set, or that allow-lists identifier characters, makes the docstring's own examples stop parsing and silently returns verified=False instead of computing.

O6_input_shapes: caret power notation: expression.replace("^", "**") before parsing (src/qwed_mcp/engines/math_engine.py:51; fix.diff:65)
two separate caller strings, expression and claimed_result, each parsed independently (fix.diff:65,82)
non-string input (e.g. a list of expressions or an int) rejected by an isinstance guard instead of being evaluated (fix.diff:229-232)
empty string and strings longer than 5000 characters rejected (fix.diff:233-239)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared normalize_math_input() helper that owns the duplicated '^' -> '**' rewrite and then calls parse_expr itself
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the identical replace() call is written out at both parse sites, so extracting it into one helper is the obvious tidy-up; if that helper parses directly it becomes a second parser sitting next to safe_parse_expr, and a solver who only edits the two call sites leaves it open.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an 'already-symbolic' fast path that runs sympify(expression) before the safe parser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sympify is imported at the pinned commit and never used; it is the usual SymPy shortcut for accepting both strings and Expr objects and looks cheaper than parse_expr, while it evaluates user text the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a restored verify_math MCP tool in tools.py forwarding expression/claimed_result/operation to the engine
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the client example still calls the removed verify_math tool and README.md:82 documents its removal in v0.2.0, so re-adding it as a thin tool wrapper with a permissive JSON schema (expression as an array) is a plausible maintainer move.

O9_family: CWE-94 code injection: eval-based SymPy parse_expr on user-controlled math expressions

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools + pyproject.toml, uv with a committed uv.lock (uv sync --locked), pip install -e ".[dev]", pytest, multi-stage Dockerfile on ubuntu 24.04
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_engines.py:7-32 TestMathEngine -- four tests (derivative correct/wrong, integral, simplify) plus a CI smoke assertion at .github/workflows/ci.yml:46-53; no test covers malicious expression input and the fix diff adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap both calls to sympy.sympify (already imported at src/qwed_mcp/engines/math_engine.py:31) or add a '__import__'-style denylist regex while leaving SymPy's default global_dict in place -- both still execute user text with full builtins.

out_of_scope_notes: tools.py execute_python_code runs LLM-supplied Python in a subprocess by design (src/qwed_mcp/tools.py:155-162), behind the QWED_MCP_TRUSTED_CODE_EXECUTION flag and the risk gateway; it is a different sink from the SymPy parse and outside this advisory.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell in this session); the tree contains ~11 source modules plus uv.lock, so it is far below 5 MB of source, which is why tiny_repo is asserted.
